classification.difficultyReason: Translate tangency into a repeated root of the intersection equation, solve the resulting quadratic in p and substitute each value back into the line equation.

content.prompt: Find the values of $p$ for which $y=px-3p-5$ is a tangent to $x^2=8y$. Hence find the equations of the tangents.

answer.short:
For $p=\frac52$, the tangent is $y=\frac52x-\frac{25}{2}$.

For $p=-1$, the tangent is $y=-x-2$.
answer.worked:
At an intersection, $x^2=8(px-3p-5)$, so $x^2-8px+24p+40=0$. A tangent meets the parabola at one point, so $\Delta=0$.

$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-8p)^2-4(1)(24p+40)\\\Delta&=64p^2-96p-160\\\Delta&=32(2p-5)(p+1)\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}(2p-5)(p+1)&=0\end{align*}$$

Thus $p=\frac52$ or $p=-1$. Substituting into the line equation gives

$$\begin{align*}y&=\tfrac52x-3\left(\tfrac52\right)-5\\y&=\tfrac52x-\tfrac{25}{2}\end{align*}$$

for $p=\frac52$, and

$$\begin{align*}y&=-x-3(-1)-5\\y&=-x-2\end{align*}$$

for $p=-1$.
